2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted a suit in the court of the Subordinate Judge, Patiya being Other Class Suit No. 17 of 1997, praying for a decree for a specific performance of the contract in respect of the suit land. The defendant opposite parties entered appearance in the suit and contested it by filing written statement. Eventually the suit was fixed for preemptory ex parte disposal as the defendant did not finally appear to contest the suit. On 18.10.98 the present petitioner filed an application before the learned Subordinate Judge under Order 1, Rule 10 C.P.C. praying for being added as a party to the suit alleging, inter alia, that he has interests in the suit property and as such his presence is necessary for an effective adjudication of the suit. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before us the impugned order dated 24.3.99 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge as well as the application under Order 1 Rule 10 C.P.C. There is no dispute to the fact that the present petitioner is not a party to the disputed deed of agreement for sale of the suit property. It is thus evident that any decree passed in the suit will not be binding upon him as he does not claim through the defendant. The petitioner claiming interests independent of the contract and independent of the defendant is not at all a necessary party in the suit as the court shall not decide the question of title in the suit. The presence of the petitioner is not necessary for an effective adjudication of the suit. The application under Order 1 Rule 10 C.P.C. is thus found to be totally misconceived in the facts of the case. 

 8. Mr. H. N. Nandi cites before us the case of Mir Hashmat Ali Vs. Birendra Kumar Ghosh and others, reported in 16, D.L.R. ((IC) 239 in support of his contention, where it has been held that the court may allow a person to be impleaded in the suit, though such person may not have interest in the suit property, if the effect of the decree in such a suit results in defeating some provisions of the existing laws and operates adversely to the Government's interest and is otherwise inequitable. We find that the principle of law enunciated in the cited case does not in any way help the petitioner. The interest of the petitioner in the suit property if may remains totally unaffected by any decree that may be passed in the suit. 

 Mr. Rabi Sankar Chakraborty, on the other hand, cites before us the case of Golam Kader and others Vs. Abdul Khaleque Chowkder and others, reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107, the case of Muzaffar Ali and another Vs. Monowara Hospital and others, reported in 51 DLR (HCD) 341, the case of Nitai Chandra Shaha Vs. M/S City Ice and Cold Storage Ltd. and others, reported in 35 DLR (HCD)60 the ratio decidendi of these decisions is that the applicant's averments in the application for addition of party setting up an independent title to the suit land disentitles him to be included as a party to the suit for the specific performance of a contract in which the real question to be determined is whether the contract for sale between the parties is a genuine one and whether on the basis thereof the plaintiff is entitled to a decree for specific performance of the contract. If the petitioner is allowed to be added as a defendant in the suit to plead his title in the suit land, this will simply convert the present suit for specific performance of the contract into a regular title suit, unnecessarily changing the nature and character of the suit. In such view of the matter, we are of the opinion that the learned Subordinate Judge was perfectly justified in rejecting the petitioner's application for addition of party under Order 1 Rule 10 C.P.C. We, therefore, find no substance if the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The revision is found without any merit and if fails accordingly.
